title: Speaker
summary: For speakers: a booking button first, the topics you speak on, recent talks with video, and what organisers need.

for: Experts who speak alongside their main work
notFor: Researchers whose talks are part of academic work (start from researcher)

cards.purpose: Two to four topics, one line each.
What organisers need: bio, photo, formats.
Recent talks, with video where it exists.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a square photo or logo for your profile picture?
slots.write: The member uploads it in the editor; never fetch one from the web.

slots.ask: How should organisers book you: a booking page, an agent, email?
slots.write: First button = the booking page (hire preset). Agent addresses only with the agent's agreement. Only an address they confirm may be public: everyone can see it.

slots.ask: What two to four topics do you speak on? One line each on the angle you take.
slots.write: A list: bold topic title, then the angle in one line.

slots.ask: What formats do you offer, do you have a speaker kit, and how do you handle fees?
slots.write: Formats, kit link and fee policy as they state them. Never publish a fee figure unless they ask.

slots.ask: Which recent talks should be listed? Links to video are best.
slots.write: tag = event · year; title as delivered; description = format and whether video exists. Audience numbers only if the event published them.

slots.ask: Where else should organisers look you up?
